title: Karsh International Scholarship
legacy_titles: Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission for international students with demonstrated financial need, administered by Duke's Office of University Scholars and Fellows and funded by the Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support
funding_type: Full cost of attendance coverage (tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, and demonstrated need above those costs) plus three summers of research/internship funding (university-funded)
administering_authority: Duke University - Office of University Scholars and Fellows (OUSF)
implementing_agency: Duke University - Office of University Scholars and Fellows in conjunction with the Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support
programme_action: Duke merit scholarship for incoming first-year students (2026-2027 admission cycle)
description: The Karsh International Scholarship was founded in 2010 at Duke University through a donation from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh to recognize the exceptional contributions international scholars make to Duke University. Duke describes Karsh International Scholars as an intellectually and civically engaged cohort of international students who promote interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research, and scholarship in the service of society. The scholarship is open to international applicants who have demonstrated financial need, and Duke states that it covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need that exceeds those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities that will advance the student's academic career. There is no separate application: applicants must apply for admission to Duke University and request financial aid at the time of application.

award_types: Karsh International Scholarship (one of Duke's merit scholarships for incoming first-year students)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: The Karsh International Scholarship is administered as one of Duke's merit scholarships for incoming first-year students alongside the Alumni Endowed Scholarship, Angier B. Duke Scholarship, Benjamin N. Duke Scholarship, Trinity Scholarships, and University Scholarship, plus the Robertson Scholars Program which does have a separate application process. Duke states that there is no separate application for merit scholarships for incoming first-year students except for the Robertson Scholars Program.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Duke states that aid awarded to international applicants is automatically renewed for subsequent years, and that financial aid requires reapplication only for current students each year, not for initial international applicants whose four-year awards are issued at admission. Renewal is tied to continued enrollment, satisfactory academic progress, and continued financial-need eligibility.
programme_structure.intake: Fall (one annual first-year intake; Duke admits for fall entry only)

status_note: The 2026-2027 admission cycle is open at the time of verification on 2026-10-03. The published deadlines are Early Decision applications due November 2, 2026 with financial aid applications (CSS Profile and FAFSA) due November 3, 2026, and Regular Decision applications due January 4, 2027 with financial aid applications due February 1, 2027. Decisions are released mid-December for Early Decision and late March/early April for Regular Decision, with aid offers released with the admission decision.
verification_notes: All core fields including the funding package, eligibility exclusions, the absence of a separate application, the 2026-2027 cost of attendance, and the 2026-2027 cycle deadlines were read directly from official duke.edu web pages. The Karsh scholarship page is published on ousf.duke.edu (Office of University Scholars and Fellows); cost of attendance, financial aid requirements, and awarding policy are published on financialaid.duke.edu (Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support); and admission cycle dates, international applicant policy, and merit scholarship selection process are published on admissions.duke.edu.
source_last_updated: 2026 (the Karsh International Scholars Program page carries a Karsh Class of 2030 cohort image with a 2026-08-22 asset timestamp)

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Early Decision applications due November 2 of the application year; Regular Decision applications due January 4 of the enrollment year
application_deadline.application_period: The Common Application is made available in early August; the CSS Profile becomes available to complete on October 1. Deadlines for the 2026-27 cycle: Early Decision application November 2, 2026; Regular Decision application January 4, 2027.
application_deadline.official_rule: Duke Undergraduate Admissions publishes Early Decision applications due November 2, 2026 with the Early Decision Agreement, high school transcript, first quarter grades, Secondary School Report with counselor recommendation, and two teacher recommendations also due November 2, 2026; financial aid applications (CSS Profile and FAFSA) are due November 3, 2026, with additional financial aid documents due November 15, 2026. Regular Decision applications are due January 4, 2027 with financial aid applications due February 1, 2027 and the midyear grade report due February 15, 2027.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The Karsh Scholarship has no separate application deadline of its own; the scholarship is decided through Duke's admission and financial aid review, so the operative deadlines are Duke's Early Decision and Regular Decision admission deadlines plus the matching financial aid application deadlines. An international applicant who does not indicate interest in financial aid in the original first-year application is ineligible for need-based financial aid at any point, which would also disqualify them from Karsh consideration.

programme_duration.official_range: Four years of undergraduate education (eight academic semesters of potential undergraduate enrollment)
programme_duration.renewal_note: Duke states it meets 100 percent of each admitted student's demonstrated need for eight academic semesters of potential undergraduate enrollment, and that international applicants receive four-year aid awards automatically renewed for subsequent years.

funding.scholarship_type: Merit scholarship for international students with demonstrated financial need, awarded at admission
funding.monthly_amount_note: Duke does not publish a monthly stipend figure for the Karsh International Scholarship. The award is structured as institutional grant aid covering billed and non-billed costs of attendance plus three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other academic opportunities.
funding.travel_amount_note: Duke states that international students receiving need-based financial aid are automatically enrolled in the Duke Student Medical Insurance plan with the charge automatically covered with grant aid. Transportation costs are budgeted for international students as one economy-class round-trip ticket per year, but no dollar amount is published for the Karsh summer funding or transportation allowance.
funding.fully_funded_note: Duke states the award covers tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, and demonstrated need that exceeds those costs, plus three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities. Duke also states it meets 100 percent of demonstrated need for eight academic semesters of potential undergraduate enrollment. Coverage is limited to documented need and the published cost of attendance; it is not an unconditional cash award.

tuition.conditions: Duke states the award covers tuition. 2026-2027 first-year tuition is $73,740 (Duke undergraduate tuition is charged the same rate for in-state and out-of-state students); this figure is the cost-of-attendance component, not the scholarship value.

room_and_board.conditions: Duke states the award covers room and board. For 2026-2027 first-year students, Duke's cost of attendance lists Housing (Double Room) at $11,560 and Food at $10,469.

mandatory_fees.conditions: Duke states the award covers mandatory fees. The 2026-2027 first-year estimated fees figure is $3,019; Engineering Dues of $60 apply to Pratt School of Engineering students only.

demonstrated_need_above_costs.conditions: Duke states the award covers demonstrated need that exceeds the billed costs of tuition, room and board, and mandatory fees. The amount is determined individually from the CSS Profile and is not published.

summer_research_funding.conditions: Duke states scholars receive three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities that will advance their academic career. Duke's merit scholarship pages describe enrichment funds available after completion of the first year to support research, internships, service work, and creative projects. No dollar cap is published.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source; Duke does not describe the Karsh International Scholarship as paying a monthly stipend.

travel_allowance.conditions: Duke's awarding policy budgets transportation for students living abroad as one economy-class round-trip ticket per year, but the dollar amount is not published.

visa_support.note: Not published as a payment benefit. Duke does state that I-20 forms for incoming foreign students are issued only after a student accepts an offer of admission and returns a completed Certificate of Financial Responsibility, and that all foreign nationals including winners of Duke merit scholarships must complete the Certificate of Financial Responsibility.

insurance.conditions: International students receiving need-based financial aid are automatically enrolled in the Duke Student Medical Insurance plan and the charge is automatically covered with grant aid.

research_allowance.conditions: Covered as part of the three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities, and the OUSF enrichment funds available after the first year.

book_allowance.conditions: Duke's 2026-2027 cost of attendance budgets $536 for Books, Course Materials, Supplies, and Equipment for a first-year undergraduate; this is an estimated cost of attendance component, not a separately disbursed Karsh allowance.

accommodation_support.conditions: Duke's 2026-2027 first-year cost of attendance budgets Housing (Double Room) at $11,560. Duke states financial aid covers on-campus housing at actual cost, so grant aid increases with a more expensive on-campus room for students receiving need-based grant aid.

bond.note: No service bond or repayment obligation is published for the Karsh International Scholarship. Students receiving need-based grants or scholarships from Duke may be asked to write thank-you letters to individual donors.

total_estimated_value.note: Duke does not publish a total scholarship value for the Karsh International Scholarship on the official Karsh page. Older Duke Today news articles (2019, 2020, 2021) state the scholarship was worth approximately or over $315,000 over four years based on estimated tuition rates, but the current official Karsh page publishes no total value, so no total is recorded here.

coverage_limitations: Duke states the award covers demonstrated need that exceeds the billed costs; the actual award amount is calculated individually from the CSS Profile and is not published as a fixed figure.

Duke states financial resources for international students are limited and that each year Duke expects to enroll only 20 to 25 international students whose full demonstrated need has been met with a university-provided need-based aid package.

Duke states international applicants who indicate interest in financial aid are considered in a more highly selective separate admission pool, and that the admit rate for foreign citizens seeking financial aid is usually less than half of the overall admit rate.

Federal loans are not available to international students, and Duke states that scholarship support in excess of tuition, books, and fees is federally taxable, with amounts used for housing and food considered taxable income.

Duke states it cannot assume financial responsibility for currency fluctuations and cannot make up foregone resources such as lost support from friends or relatives or a decision to decline outside aid.

Duke states that international applicants admitted with 'no financial aid interest' are ineligible to apply for financial aid for any year of undergraduate study, and that international transfer students are not eligible for need-based or merit scholarships.

Exact benefit structure, renewal terms, and summer funding amounts may differ by individual award and are confirmed only in the individual aid offer; the individual cost of attendance is listed on the student's aid offer.
Duke's cost of attendance figures are estimates before financial aid is applied and vary by student housing and meal plan selections.
eligible_applicants: Citizens of countries outside the United States (Duke confirms a student who is a citizen of any country outside the U.S. can be considered)
International applicants who demonstrate documented financial need and complete the financial aid forms
International applicants with strong academic preparation who are admitted as first-year students through Duke's admission process
final_year_condition: For this first-year bachelor's entry scholarship, applicants are students completing secondary school: Duke requires a high school transcript and first-quarter or midyear grades from the applicant's high school, so applicants in their final year of secondary school are eligible. Duke states a high school diploma or GED is required for admission.
equivalent_degree_note: Duke states a high school diploma or GED is required for admission and that homeschooled and online-schooled applicants need no additional application requirements, so equivalent secondary-school credentials are accepted. Duke states a student who already has a B.A. or B.S. degree cannot be considered for this scholarship.

eligibility.citizenship: Must be a citizen of a country outside the United States. Duke's FAQ confirms students with dual U.S./other country citizenship cannot be considered, and that students who already hold a B.A. or B.S. degree cannot be considered.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement beyond being admitted to Duke University as a first-year undergraduate student.
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit published by Duke for first-year undergraduate admission or for the Karsh International Scholarship.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Completion of secondary school is required. Duke requires a high school transcript, a Secondary School Report with counselor recommendation, two teacher recommendations, and first-quarter grades for Early Decision applicants or a midyear grade report by February 15 for Regular Decision applicants.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Duke states strong academic preparation is what makes a good candidate for this scholarship. Duke describes a holistic review that considers academic and personal interests, accomplishments, and unique experiences, perspectives, and background. Duke recommends four years of English and at least three years of mathematics, natural sciences, world language, and social studies.
eligibility.language_requirement: English proficiency tests are recommended but not required for non-native English speakers or applicants not currently studying in an English-medium curriculum. Duke publishes expected minimum scores of 180 for Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency, 130 for Duolingo, band 7 for IELTS, 70 for PTE Academic, 100 for the internet-based TOEFL and 75 for the revised TOEFL paper-delivered test. Duke states testing policies are the same for all applicants with no additional requirements for international students.
eligibility.work_experience: No prior work experience is required. Duke states that unpaid internships are among the opportunities the summer funding supports.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: No formal extracurricular requirement, but Duke reviews up to 10 extracurricular activities and states it is more interested in sustained commitment than a long list. Duke states scholars engage in faculty-led enrichment, research, service work, and creative projects after their first year.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: No separate leadership requirement is published for Karsh. The Office of University Scholars and Fellows describes merit scholars as contributing to a community of ambitious and collegial thinkers and states finalists interview with scholarship selection committees.
eligibility.financial_need: Yes, required. Duke states international applicants must have demonstrated financial need to be eligible for this scholarship and that applicants must apply to Duke University and request financial aid.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Not published for this scholarship. Duke states international students admitted who did not check the financial aid interest box on the admissions application are ineligible to apply for financial aid for any year of undergraduate study.
eligibility.previous_award_restriction: Not published for this scholarship. Duke states international students admitted who did not check the financial aid interest box on the admissions application are ineligible to apply for financial aid for any year of undergraduate study, which would remove Karsh eligibility.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Applicants must be entering Duke as first-year undergraduate students. Duke states a student who already has a B.A. or B.S. degree cannot be considered, and students who have already completed an undergraduate bachelor's degree at a four-year college cannot be considered for transfer admission.
eligibility.health_requirement: No health requirement published. Duke requires all registered students to have health insurance; international students receiving need-based aid are automatically enrolled in the Duke Student Medical Insurance plan with the charge covered by grant aid.
eligibility.field_restrictions: No field of study restriction. Applicants apply through either Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering; Duke states it is not easier or harder to be admitted to one program than the other.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: Duke publishes no minimum GPA or percentage threshold for first-year undergraduate admission or for the Karsh International Scholarship.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Pratt School of Engineering applicants must have coursework in calculus, and physics is strongly recommended. Duke recommends four years of English and at least three years of mathematics, natural sciences, world language, and social studies.
selection_factors_may_include: Potential for academic and global impact
Commitment to interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research, and scholarship in the service of society
Recommendations from two teachers and a school counselor
Essays including the Common Application personal essay and Duke short-answer questions
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Duke states that its holistic approach considers both academic and personal interests, what the applicant has accomplished, and unique experiences, perspectives, and background. Duke states that merit scholarship eligibility is determined on the basis of the applicant's application to Duke University.

english_requirement.moi_rule: Duke states English proficiency tests are recommended but not required for non-native English speakers or applicants not currently studying in an English-medium curriculum. No medium-of-instruction waiver is published.
english_requirement.test_score_note: Duke states these are expected minimum scores, not strict cutoffs, that English proficiency tests are recommended but not required, that the highest score is used if the test is taken more than once, and that Duke has no preference among English proficiency tests. For the TOEFL paper-delivered test the minimum expected score is 75; for Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency the minimum expected score is 180.
accepted_tests: TOEFL including TOEFL Home Edition (minimum expected 100 on the internet-based TOEFL; 75 on the revised TOEFL paper-delivered test)

language_of_instruction.language_note: Instruction at Duke University is in English. Duke states that applicants not currently studying in an English-medium curriculum are recommended but not required to take an English proficiency test.

application_method.application_route: Applicants must apply for admission to Duke University through the Common Application (or the QuestBridge Application for eligible students) and request financial aid by checking the financial aid interest box; there is no separate application for the Karsh International Scholarship.
application_steps: Create and submit the Common Application (or QuestBridge Application for eligible students), applying to either Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering, and select Early Decision or Regular Decision.

Ensure the application for undergraduate admission indicates 'yes' in the financial aid interest box; if it was not initially checked, contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions to change the designation.
Pay or waive the non-refundable $85 application fee (Duke offers fee waivers for qualifying students with high financial need, requestable through the Common Application).

Ask the school counselor to submit the Secondary School Report with counselor recommendation and the high school transcript, and ask two teachers of major academic courses to submit recommendations (three recommendations are required in total; for Pratt School of Engineering applicants at least one should be from a math or science teacher).
Write the one-page Common Application personal essay and answer the required Duke short-essay questions (250 words each) for the 2026-27 cycle.

Optionally self-report SAT or ACT scores (Duke is test-optional for the 2026-2027 cycle), optionally submit an arts supplement through SlideRoom, and optionally arrange an InitialView interview or record a Glimpse video.

Complete the 2026-27 CSS Profile Application online at cssprofile.collegeboard.org by the financial aid deadline (available to complete from October 1); U.S. citizens and permanent residents must also submit the FAFSA, but non-U.S. citizens and permanent residents may skip the FAFSA.

Submit any additional financial aid documents requested through the College Board's IDOC service, and for international applicants provide the family's most recent foreign tax forms converted into US dollars and an English-language statement from both parents' employers stating annual income (with an officially translated English copy and the currency exchange noted).
For Early Decision, submit first-quarter grades by November 2 and any additional financial aid documents by November 15. For Regular Decision, submit the midyear grade report by February 15.

Wait for the admission and financial aid decision (released mid-December for Early Decision and late March/early April for Regular Decision) and, if selected as a merit scholarship finalist, complete the interview with the scholarship selection committee.

Upon admission, complete the Certificate of Financial Responsibility and, after enrolling, attend the mandatory international financial aid session and complete the Foreign National Form and payroll certification.

selection_process.decision_maker: Duke Office of Undergraduate Admissions, with merit scholarship decisions by the Duke Office of University Scholars and Fellows and financial need determined by the Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support
selection_process.selection_type: Automatic consideration at admission; merit scholarship finalists are interviewed by scholarship selection committees
possible_stages: Admission application reviewed holistically by the Duke admissions committee (international aid applicants reviewed in a separate, more highly selective pool)
Financial need determined by the Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support from the CSS Profile and supporting documents
Aid package built to meet demonstrated need and released with the offer of admission (mid-December for Early Decision; late March to early April for Regular Decision)

selection_process.weighting_note: Duke does not publish a numerical weighting of selection criteria for the Karsh International Scholarship. Duke states that what makes a good candidate is strong academic preparation and documented need for financial aid, and that the amount of need-based financial aid a student qualifies for depends solely on financial calculations and not on the strength of the admissions application.
selection_process.results_timing: Early Decision aid offers are released in mid-December with the admission decision; Regular Decision aid offers are released in late March to early April. Merit scholarship finalists are notified in the spring and awarded shortly after their interviews.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Duke describes the Karsh International Scholarship as one of several merit scholarships for incoming first-year students, granted on the basis of the applicant's application to Duke University, and states that the Karsh International Scholarship recognizes the outstanding potential for academic and global impact of international students.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree from Duke University through Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Four years (eight academic semesters of potential undergraduate enrollment)
degree_outcome.degree_note: Duke states it meets 100 percent of each admitted student's demonstrated need for eight academic semesters of potential undergraduate enrollment, and that first-year applicants must choose either Trinity College of Arts & Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Duke states it awards a limited amount of course credit and advanced placement on the basis of scores earned on Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, and pre-matriculation college coursework, with credit granted only after admission and evaluation by the Registrar's Office.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Covered by the scholarship; Duke states the award covers tuition, room and board, and mandatory fees, and that financial aid covers on-campus housing at actual cost with grant aid increased for a more expensive on-campus room.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: The $85 application fee is waived for qualifying students with high financial need through the Common Application fee waiver request, endorsed by the school counselor.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: All Duke students must agree to the Conditions of Application, the Community Standard, and financial aid terms and conditions. Students receiving need-based grants or scholarships from Duke may be asked to write thank-you letters to individual donors.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Duke states that students whose total credits exceed their total charges receive a refund of the difference, that Duke offers a monthly payment plan through Nelnet, that Parent PLUS loans are available to parents of admitted students, and that federal loans are not available to international students. International students receiving need-based aid are automatically enrolled in the Duke Student Medical Insurance plan with the charge covered by grant aid, and local transportation is provided through free passes to the Duke and Durham city bus system.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No bond or service obligation is published for the Karsh International Scholarship.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Not applicable; no bond or service obligation is published.

application_readiness_checklist: Check the financial aid interest box in the Common Application (mandatory for any aid eligibility at Duke)

Gather the family's most recent foreign tax returns and English-language employer income statements for both parents, plus official translations with USD conversion
Have the school counselor submit the Secondary School Report and high school transcript directly
Confirm two teachers and the counselor are submitting recommendations through the Common Application

programme_comparison_fields.award_scope: Full cost of attendance plus summer funding
programme_comparison_fields.citizenship_restriction: Non-U.S. citizens only (dual U.S. citizenship excluded)

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: Duke requires a Common Application personal essay plus two required 250-word Duke short essays ('Why Duke' and 'Communities') and one optional 250-word essay. Because Karsh selects for intellectual and civic engagement and for potential for global impact, the 'Communities' essay and the optional 'Viewpoints and experiences' essay are the natural places to evidence service, civic engagement, and a documented record of interdisciplinary curiosity. Duke does not accept separate resumes, research abstracts, or media files, so achievements must be framed inside the essays and the 10 activity slots.
common_mistakes: Assuming a separate Karsh application exists (Duke states there is no separate application; the applicant must simply apply to Duke and request financial aid)
Forgetting to check the financial aid interest box in the admissions application, which permanently removes eligibility for need-based aid at Duke

Assuming applying for need-based aid does not affect international admission chances (Duke states international aid applicants are reviewed in a separate, more highly selective pool with an admit rate usually less than half the overall rate)
Missing that Early Decision is binding and that the Early Decision aid deadline (November 3) differs from the Regular Decision aid deadline (February 1)
Submitting a separate resume or abstract, which Duke does not accept
Assuming FAFSA is required (Duke states non-U.S. citizens and permanent residents may skip the FAFSA but must complete the CSS Profile)
Assuming English proficiency scores are required (they are recommended but not required)
Assuming federal loans are available to international students (Duke states they are not)

risk_flags.risk: International applicants requiring financial aid are reviewed in a separate, more highly selective admission pool with an admit rate usually less than half of Duke's overall admit rate
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the Karsh Scholarship as highly competitive; present the strongest possible academic record and compelling evidence of civic engagement, and do not rely on Duke as a single application

risk_flags.risk: Duke states financial resources for international students are limited and it expects to enroll only 20 to 25 international students each year whose full demonstrated need is met with university-provided need-based aid
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply broadly to other fully funded scholarships and universities; be prepared to fund a substantial portion of the cost of attendance from other sources

risk_flags.risk: Failing to check the financial aid interest box in the original first-year application permanently removes eligibility for need-based aid and therefore Karsh consideration
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the box at submission; if it was missed, contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions immediately to change the designation

risk_flags.risk: Scholarship funds in excess of tuition, books, and fees are federally taxable, and amounts used for housing and food count as taxable income for international students
risk_flags.mitigation: Consult a tax preparer on U.S. tax obligations for international students, file a U.S. income tax return upon receiving the 1042S, and obtain an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)

risk_flags.risk: Federal loans are unavailable to international students and Duke cannot assume responsibility for currency fluctuations or foregone outside resources
risk_flags.mitigation: Plan a funding strategy that does not depend on U.S. federal borrowing and that accounts for exchange-rate movement

risk_flags.risk: Deadline timing differs between the admission deadline and the financial aid deadline within the same decision plan
risk_flags.mitigation: Diary all four dates: ED application 2026-11-02 and ED aid 2026-11-03; RD application 2027-01-04 and RD aid 2027-02-01, plus first-quarter grades and midyear grade reports

risk_flags.risk: The 2026-2027 cost of attendance figures published on the financial aid site differ from the 2025-2026 figures still shown in some places, and the individual cost of attendance is confirmed only on the student's aid offer
risk_flags.mitigation: Use the 2026-2027 figures on the official cost of attendance page and confirm the final figures on the individual aid offer

risk_flags.risk: Award eligibility requires continued enrollment and satisfactory academic progress, and renewal depends on continued need
risk_flags.mitigation: Maintain full-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress, and reappear financial information as required for renewal

application_status_workflow: Apply to Duke (Common App or QuestBridge) with financial aid interest indicated
Submit CSS Profile and requested financial documents
Admission review in separate international aid applicant pool
Merit scholarship finalist notification and interview (spring)
Certificate of Financial Responsibility completed upon admission
Enroll and attend mandatory international financial aid session
Aid renewed annually for subsequent years
best_fit: Non-U.S. citizen high school students with strong academic records and documented financial need who want a fully funded undergraduate degree at a highly selective U.S. university, and who can commit to Duke's need-aware admission pool for aided international applicants, complete the CSS Profile on time, and are willing to be considered for a scholarship interview as finalists.
not_best_fit: U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or dual U.S./other-country citizens (Duke states dual U.S./other-country citizens cannot be considered)
Students who already hold a B.A. or B.S. degree
Transfer applicants (Duke states there are no need-based or merit scholarships for international transfer students)
Students who cannot demonstrate financial need
Students unwilling to indicate financial aid interest at the time of application
Students seeking a separate scholarship application process or a scholarship that does not require a full admission application
Applicants who need federal student loans to fund their studies

No rights statement is published for these assets.

database_notes: No substitution was needed: the Duke University Karsh International Scholarship is not on the DO-NOT-DUPLICATE list in research/bachelor/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md.
All research was conducted on official duke.edu subdomains only (ousf.duke.edu, financialaid.duke.edu, admissions.duke.edu). No aggregator sources such as scholarshipsinstitute.com were used.

The Karsh International Scholarship is administered by the Duke Office of University Scholars and Fellows (ousf.duke.edu), with financial need determined by the Karsh Office of Undergraduate Financial Support (financialaid.duke.edu, formerly the Office of Undergraduate Financial Aid).

Deadline dates: the official admissions checklist and Apply page state 'November 2' for Early Decision and 'January 4' for Regular Decision for the 2026-2027 admission cycle, and the counselors page labels these as 'NOV 2, 2026' and 'JAN 4, 2027'. The Apply for Aid page states the financial aid deadlines as 'November 3' for Early Decision and 'February 1' for Regular Decision. These are therefore recorded as 2026-11-02, 2027-01-04, 2026-11-03 and 2027-02-01.

Time zone: no official duke.edu page read during this research states a clock time or time zone for the application or financial aid deadlines. deadline_timezone is therefore recorded as null rather than inferred, and this is listed as an item to check.

The official Karsh page states the award covers 'your tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need that exceeds those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities that will advance your academic career.' This exact wording is the basis of the funding_breakdown.

Cost of attendance figures are the 2026-2027 first-year undergraduate figures published at https://financialaid.duke.edu/how-aid-calculated/cost-attendance/. The financial aid site's Awarding & Policy page still displays 2025-2026 figures; the 2026-2027 figures were used as the current cycle. These are cost-of-attendance estimates before aid, not the scholarship value.

No total four-year value is published on the official Karsh page. Duke Today articles from 2019, 2020 and 2021 state approximately or over $315,000 over four years based on estimated tuition rates, but because the current official page publishes no total value, no total is recorded in funding_breakdown.total_estimated_value.

Duke's official pages do not publish a fixed number of Karsh International Scholarships awarded per cycle. Duke does state that financial resources for international students are limited and that it expects to enroll 20 to 25 international students each year whose full demonstrated need is met with university-provided need-based aid, and that international applicants admitted with 'no financial aid interest' are ineligible for aid.

Duke states the financial aid interest box must be checked in the original first-year application, and that international applicants may contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions to change this designation if it was not initially checked. This is recorded as a critical application requirement rather than a scholarship-specific rule.

A logo asset could not be verified for the Karsh International Scholarship. The favicon assets on ousf.duke.edu returned HTTP 200 but are generic Duke site icons rather than a Karsh or OUSF logo, and no brand-guidelines page was found, so logo_url and image_url are null. This is an accepted honest outcome under the logo rules.

English proficiency minimum scores are what Duke states are 'expected' minimums for tests that Duke describes as 'recommended but not required'. They are recorded as published, with the universal requirement set to false.

Duration is recorded as four years because Duke states it meets 100 percent of demonstrated need for eight academic semesters of potential undergraduate enrollment and that four-year aid awards are issued to international applicants.

Status is OPEN because the 2026-2027 cycle deadlines (November 2026 and January/February 2027) are in the future as of the verification date of 2026-10-03, and because the Common Application and CSS Profile are open.
